questions.stem: What is an Architectural Decision Record (ADR)?

options.text: A document that captures an important architectural decision along with its context and consequences.
A record of all bugs found in the software.
A list of all features to be implemented in the next release.
A document detailing the user interface design.

questions.explanation: An ADR is specifically used to document architectural decisions, providing context and outlining the consequences of those decisions. It is not related to bugs, features, or UI design.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes technical debt?

options.text: The cost of implementing new features.
The implied cost of additional rework caused by choosing an easy solution now instead of a better approach that would take longer.
The financial cost of purchasing new software tools.
The time spent on debugging software.

questions.explanation: Technical debt refers to the future cost of rework due to shortcuts taken during development. It is not directly related to financial costs or debugging time.

questions.stem: Why might a team choose to incur technical debt?

options.text: To reduce the quality of the software.
To meet a critical deadline.
To increase the complexity of the codebase.
To avoid using best practices.

questions.explanation: Teams may incur technical debt to meet critical deadlines, accepting future rework as a trade-off. It is not done to reduce quality or increase complexity intentionally.

questions.stem: A software project incurs technical debt that will require an additional 100 hours of work to resolve in the future. If the current hourly rate is $50, what is the monetary cost of this technical debt? Provide your answer in dollars.
questions.explanation: The monetary cost of technical debt is calculated by multiplying the additional hours required by the hourly rate. Here, 100 hours at $50 per hour results in a cost of $5000.

questions.stem: What is a key benefit of documenting architectural decisions?

options.text: It eliminates the need for future decision-making.
It helps future developers understand the rationale behind decisions.
It reduces the overall cost of the project.
It ensures that all decisions are optimal.

questions.explanation: Documenting architectural decisions provides context and rationale, aiding future developers in understanding past choices. It does not eliminate decision-making or guarantee optimal decisions.
